properties.name: OBSERVED 2026-09-28: served advice says `reflow2-mcp setup remote …`, which is "command not found" on a machine installed from a checkout (only `reflow2` is on PATH); and a person already signed in to flo2.io by browser through Claude Code still had to paste a key, because setup's browser sign-in is unbuilt
properties.source: who:ajs's terminal, dev_reflow2 hub session 2026-09-28; grep of crates/ at the #620 branch
properties.statement:
Two observations from one step in the dev_reflow2 hub, 2026-09-28, both on the way to letting the hub watch flo2 at its address.

1. THE ADVICE NAMES A COMMAND THAT IS NOT THERE. upstream_status answered flo2's 401 with "`reflow2-mcp setup remote https://api.flo2.io` stores one in the OS keychain". Anthony ran exactly that and got `reflow2-mcp: command not found`. This machine was installed from a checkout: tools/reflow2_install.py put only a `reflow2` wrapper in ~/.local/bin, which execs target/release/reflow2-mcp for anything it does not handle itself, and no `reflow2-mcp` is on PATH. `reflow2 setup remote https://api.flo2.io` worked first time ("Connected: 8 designs there. key: in the OS keychain"). 16 places in crates/ name `reflow2-mcp setup` in text (pointer.rs, client_setup.rs, upstream.rs, service.rs, mcp_http.rs, main.rs, one test). Not walked: whether a release install puts `reflow2-mcp` on PATH, and which name served advice should use.

2. A BROWSER SIGN-IN DID NOT CARRY OVER. Anthony had signed in to flo2 by browser through Claude Code's /mcp, and asked why a key was needed at all. That sign-in belongs to Claude Code's connection; the hub's own reflow2 server calls api.flo2.io separately and has no credential of its own. This requirement says setup signs in "by browser for a server that offers it, or with a key", and only the key half is built (client_setup.rs: "Browser sign-in is a later step; the shape leaves room for it as another `KeySource`").
